explanation: The `instance` field is not declared `volatile`. In the double-checked locking pattern, the write `instance = new Singleton()` is not guaranteed to be atomic with respect to visibility — the JVM/CPU can reorder the write of the reference to `instance` ahead of the constructor finishing initializing the object's fields. Without `volatile`, a second thread that reads `instance` in the outer `if` check (outside the synchronized block) can see a non-null reference to an object whose fields haven't finished being set, and start using a partially-constructed Singleton. Declaring `instance` as `volatile` establishes a happens-before edge that prevents this reordering.
prompt: This lazy-initialized singleton uses the classic double-checked locking pattern. What's the bug?
choices: The `instance` field is not declared `volatile`, so a thread can observe a non-null but partially constructed object due to instruction reordering
The outer null check is redundant and should be removed for correctness
The synchronized block should synchronize on `this` instead of `Singleton.class`
The double null-check pattern will cause a deadlock when two threads call `getInstance()` simultaneously
The method should return a new instance every time instead of caching one
